sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your Twenties, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your Twenties》，这是一个探讨我们在20多岁时所面临的重大生活改变与转型，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么的播客。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身在世界的哪个角落，非常高兴你能回来收听新的一集，和我们一起剖析20多岁时的心理学。

sentences.en: Today, we're talking about something that we've actually never spoken about on the podcast before, which is honestly shocking because when it comes to our 20s,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要谈论一个我们在播客中从未谈过的话题，老实说这挺让人震惊的，因为当我们谈到20多岁时，

sentences.en: one of the universal, relatable, joint experiences of people during this decade is living with other people, is the share house, communal living, flatting,
sentences.zh: 在这个十年里，大家都有的一种普遍的、能引起共鸣的共同经历，就是和别人一起住，也就是合租屋、集体生活、合租公寓，

sentences.en: whatever you want to call it.
sentences.zh: 随便你怎么称呼它。

sentences.en: And a lot about that experience is deeply psychological, how we learn to live with others, how we communicate, our relationships, the conflict, the tension,
sentences.zh: 这种经历的很大一部分具有深刻的心理学意义，我们如何学会与他人相处、如何沟通、我们的关系、冲突、紧张气氛，

sentences.en: the psychology is really everywhere in that dynamic.
sentences.zh: 在这种动态中，心理学可以说是无处不在。

sentences.en: I think our 20s are often that time for many of us when we take the leap to move out of our childhood home, our family home, and really forge kind of our own independent lives.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于我们中的很多人来说，20多岁通常是那个让我们迈出跨越性的一步，搬离童年时代的长效家宅、家庭住宅，真正开启某种独立生活的时期。

sentences.en: It's a huge hallmark of this decade.
sentences.zh: 这是这个十年的一大标志。

sentences.en: I guess we just outgrow the family environment.
sentences.zh: 我想我们只是超越了家庭环境。

sentences.en: We don't feel like a child anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们不再觉得自己是个孩子了。

sentences.en: We want our own space.
sentences.zh: 我们想要属于自己的空间。

sentences.en: And often the most kind of economically viable option is to move in with a group of other people our own age.
sentences.zh: 而且通常在经济上最可行的选择就是和一群同龄人合租。

sentences.en: I think not only is that sometimes the only thing we can afford, let's be real, but a lot of this is that these are people that we share the same lifestyle with.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这不仅有时是我们唯一负担得起的事，说实话，很大程度上也是因为这些人与我们有着相同的生活方式。

sentences.en: And it's kind of like a rite of passage, such a valuable social experience to see how we live with others, to maybe make lifelong friends, to build our own community
sentences.zh: 这就像是一种成长仪式，是一种非常宝贵的社会经验，让我们看看自己是如何与他人生活的，也许还能结交一生的朋友，建立属于我们自己的社区，

sentences.en: that is separate from the family unit.
sentences.zh: 一个独立于家庭单位之外的社区。

sentences.en: But it's also not that straightforward.
sentences.zh: 但这也没有那么简单。

sentences.en: I've been living in share houses or dorms with roommates since I was 17.
sentences.zh: 我从17岁起就一直住在合租房或室友宿舍里。

sentences.en: So for the last seven years, that is way too long.
sentences.zh: 所以过去的七年里一直是这样，时间真的太长了。

sentences.en: And of course, I think like anyone who has done their time,
sentences.zh: 当然，我想任何经历过这段时间的人都一样，

sentences.en: I have some stories.
sentences.zh: 我也有一些故事要讲。

sentences.en: We might, you know, romanticize this way of living and the chaos and the group dinners and the movie nights, whatever it may be.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会，你知道的，把这种生活方式浪漫化，比如混乱的场面、集体晚餐、电影之夜，无论具体是什么。

sentences.en: But the people we choose to live with are sometimes the most important people in our lives.
sentences.zh: 但我们选择与之同住的人有时却是我们生命中最重要的人。

sentences.en: And so it's kind of make or break depending on how well we actually get along.
sentences.zh: 因此，这在很大程度上取决于我们实际相处得有多好，成败在此一举。

sentences.en: We are sharing a home together, which if you think about it, is like the most sacred space that a human can have.
sentences.zh: 我们在同一个屋檐下分享一个家，如果你仔细想想，这就像是人类能够拥有的最神圣的空间。

sentences.en: It is our place of comfort, of safety, of security.
sentences.zh: 这是我们感到舒适、安全和有保障的地方。

sentences.en: We sleep under the same roof as these people.
sentences.zh: 我们和这些人睡在同一个屋檐下。

sentences.en: We see them constantly and their choices impact our quality of life.
sentences.zh: 我们经常见到他们，他们的选择会影响我们的生活质量。

sentences.en: There was actually one piece of research published on this in 2016 and it indicates that the people who we live with impact everything from our eating habits, our exercise habits,
sentences.zh: 事实上，2016年有一项关于这方面的研究发表，表明我们与之同住的人会影响从我们的饮食习惯、运动习惯，

sentences.en: our sleeping habits in both a positive and a negative direction, particularly through things like peer pressure or observational learning and the adoption of like communal values.
sentences.zh: 到睡眠习惯的方方面面，既有积极的影响也有消极的影响，尤其是通过同辈压力、观察学习以及采纳集体价值观等方式。

sentences.en: And depending on your experience, that can actually be really great.
sentences.zh: 根据你的经历，这其实可以是一件非常棒的事情。

sentences.en: We can become really thick and fast friends.
sentences.zh: 我们可以成为无话不谈的生死之交。

sentences.en: For example, in Korea, they surveyed nearly a thousand young single adults living in share housing and they found that people who were living with a roommate reported feeling
sentences.zh: 例如，在韩国，他们调查了近千名居住在合租房里的年轻单身成年人，发现与室友同住的人报告说，

sentences.en: less lonely and more socially supported.
sentences.zh: 他们感到不那么孤独，得到了更多的社会支持。

sentences.en: So there are definitely a lot of benefits.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对有很多好处。

sentences.en: But when that turns sour, when we're met with conflict, different personalities, different standards for cleanliness,
sentences.zh: 但是当关系变坏时，当我们面临冲突、不同的个性、对清洁的不同标准时，

sentences.en: when we move in with friends and we begin to see a different side of someone, now that we share a bathroom or a kitchen with them, that is when I think the share house
sentences.zh: 当我们和朋友合租，开始看到某人不同的一面，现在我们要和他们共用一个浴室或厨房时，我认为合租屋就在那时

sentences.en: truly becomes a real like psychological petri dish.
sentences.zh: 真正变成了一个现实中的心理学培养皿。

sentences.en: Conflict or tension in a home has a massive effect on our mental well-being and there have been so many studies, articles, research projects on this, particularly amongst
sentences.zh: 家里的冲突或紧张气氛对我们的心理健康有着巨大的影响，已经有很多关于这方面的研究、文章和研究项目，特别是在年轻人当中，

sentences.en: young adults because if you think about it, you're basically putting two, three, four, sometimes more people together in a small environment, all of whom have different
sentences.zh: 因为如果你仔细想想，你基本上是把两、三个、四个月，有时更多的人塞进一个小环境中，所有人都有着不同的

sentences.en: backgrounds, expectations, lifestyles, and we're just kind of praying that it works and so a share house is kind of its own social experiment on how relationships are formed,
sentences.zh: 背景、期望、生活方式，而我们只是在祈祷它能管用，所以合租屋本身就像是一个关于关系如何形成、

sentences.en: how we communicate, how we interact, how relationships break down and that is really what I want to explore today.
sentences.zh: 我们如何沟通、我们如何互动、关系如何破裂的社会实验，这确实是我今天要探讨的内容。

sentences.en: We are going to discuss what makes a good roommate, different types of roommates, the four different types of roommates and living styles, the dilemma of kind of moving in
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论是什么造就了一个好室友、不同类型的室友、四种不同类型的室友和生活方式、与朋友合租的困境，

sentences.en: with friends and also what causes social harmony to break down when you are in a share house.
sentences.zh: 以及当身处合租屋时是什么导致了社会和谐的破裂。

sentences.en: I also want to talk about what psychology has to say about creating a positive space, being a good roommate, dealing with conflict in the home and also being able to recognise that
sentences.zh: 我还想谈谈心理学对于创造积极空间、做一个好室友、处理家庭冲突以及能够识别

sentences.en: moment when it is time to move out, when it is time to live alone.
sentences.zh: 是时候搬出去、是时候独自生活的那一刻有什么看法。

sentences.en: I think I'm getting to that point now.
sentences.zh: 我想我快要到那个点了。

sentences.en: I've done my time, I've done my hours, I've had the share house experience and I really just want to come home and not talk to anyone at this point.
sentences.zh: 我的时间熬够了，时数攒够了，合租的经历也体验过了，现在我真的只想回到家里，谁也不想理。

sentences.en: I kind of want to watch whatever I want to watch on TV and not have to like time my showers around other people so I think I might only have like a few more months to
sentences.zh: 我只想在电视上看我想看的东西，而不必掐着时间跟别人错开洗澡，所以我想我可能只有几个月的时间，

sentences.en: actually be able to talk about this properly from like a lived experience and that's what we're going to do today.
sentences.zh: 还能以过来人的亲身经历来好好谈论这个话题，这就是我们今天要做的。

sentences.en: So without further ado, I think it's about time we break down all of the psychology to do with communal living, share houses and roommates.
sentences.zh: 所以废话不多说，我想是时候剖析所有关于集体生活、合租屋和室友的心理学了。

sentences.en: So let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 让我们切入正题。

sentences.en: The move to share housing from the family home, whether you're living with complete strangers or friends, whoever, it's really exciting.
sentences.zh: 从原生家庭搬到合租房，无论你是和完全的陌生人还是朋友一起住，不管是谁，这都非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: Like we can't overstate the anticipation and like fun of getting to buy your own bowls and picking out your bedsheets and being able to have a space that is your own and separate
sentences.zh: 我们怎么强调这种期待感都不为过，买自己的碗、挑床单、拥有一个属于自己且独立于

sentences.en: from your parents and your siblings, whoever else is in your house.
sentences.zh: 父母和兄弟姐妹以及家中其他任何人的空间，这种乐趣是无与伦比的。

sentences.en: It honestly just feels like super adult.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这感觉超级成熟。

sentences.en: It's like one of those experiences I think we look at and we're like, oh yeah, this is the point where I felt like I was actually mature enough to call myself an adult
sentences.zh: 这就像是那种让我们觉得“哦，对啊，正是在这个时候，我觉得自己真的成熟到可以称之为一个成年人了”的经历，然后我觉得它的社交元素也超级吸引人，

sentences.en: human being and then I think the social element of it is also super appealing, especially when you live with friends.
sentences.zh: 特别是当你和朋友合租的时候。

sentences.en: It's like summer camp or a sleep over every night of the week and it's the freedom that many of us I think have been aspiring towards since we were children.
sentences.zh: 这就像每周每晚都在夏令营或过夜派对，这也是我们许多人从孩提时代起就一直渴望的自由。

sentences.en: You know, it's kind of similar to having your own money.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这有点类似于拥有自己的钱。

sentences.en: You get a space where you can live your life exactly how you would like it.
sentences.zh: 你拥有了一个可以完全按照自己喜欢的方式生活的空间。

sentences.en: So I have this theory that the first six months of communal living are like the honeymoon period.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一个理论，集体生活的前六个月就像是蜜月期。

sentences.en: It is the buzz of new things, of new relationships or at least a new dimension to a relationship if you're living with friends and this really new environment.
sentences.zh: 那是新事物带来的兴奋感，新关系的兴奋感，或者至少是如果你和朋友同住时关系的一种新维度，以及这个全新的环境。

sentences.en: But I think after that six months period is when the reality of like constantly having to share your space with someone who is not related to you sinks in.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在那六个月的时期之后，不得不不断与一个没有血缘关系的人分享空间的现实才真正显现出来。

sentences.en: The biggest thing we have to adapt to is different living styles because each of us has grown up in a certain unique environment expecting certain levels of different rules
sentences.zh: 我们必须适应的最大事情是不同的生活方式，因为我们每个人都在某个独特的环境中长大，期望有不同规则的水平、

sentences.en: times that we want to rest times that we want to socialize people just use their spaces differently.
sentences.zh: 我们想休息的时间、想社交的时间，大家对空间的使用方式各不相同。

sentences.en: They treat them differently based on the home environment of their childhood.
sentences.zh: 他们根据童年的家庭环境以不同的方式对待空间。

sentences.en: It's really interesting because there's been research on this and it's shown that how your parents organized a home is going to be one of the biggest determinants for
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣，因为这方面有过研究，结果表明你的父母如何整理家务将是你决定

sentences.en: how you choose to treat your future living spaces and it is natural normal for those there to be kind of differences across people.
sentences.zh: 如何对待未来生活空间的最大决定因素之一，而人与人之间存在某种差异是自然且正常的。

sentences.en: The biggest one for me is the level of mess that we are willing to tolerate.
sentences.zh: 对我来说最重要的一点是我们愿意容忍的凌乱程度。

sentences.en: I have noticed this in my own share houses and with my roommates where there is a distinction between wanting things tidy and wanting things clean.
sentences.zh: 我在我自己的合租房里和室友身上注意到了这一点，那就是“希望东西整洁（tidy）”和“希望东西干净（clean）”是有区别的。

sentences.en: Some people just don't care if the floors aren't vacuumed or the couches are a little bit dirty as long as there are like no personal items in a communal space but others
sentences.zh: 有些人根本不在乎地板有没有吸尘，或者沙发是不是有点脏，只要公共空间里没有个人物品就行；但另一些人

sentences.en: are totally fine with like a certain level of untidiness as long as the house is sanitized and then there are the housemates the unique housemates who just don't care who are happy
sentences.zh: 则完全可以接受一定程度的杂乱，只要房子是经过卫生消毒的；然后还有那些独特的室友，他们根本不在乎，乐于

sentences.en: to live in absolute squalor.
sentences.zh: 生活在绝对的藏污纳垢中。

sentences.en: I often see this as a reaction to three things.
sentences.zh: 我经常认为这是对三件事的一种反应。

sentences.en: Firstly for these individuals who really don't care about mess or cleanliness that was the standard that their parents set whereby they also didn't really care about living amongst
